name: Lateral anterolateral approach to the distal femur
region: lateral distal thigh and distal femur
corridor: Lateral iliotibial-band incision with distal-to-proximal vastus-lateralis elevation and optional lateral arthrotomy

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with a bump under the ipsilateral hip and the knee flexed enough to relax gastrocnemius and permit lateral imaging.

setup.text: Prepare the entire limb, review CT for articular extensions, plan plate length, and ensure unobstructed AP, lateral, and oblique imaging.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark femoral shaft, lateral epicondyle, joint line, patella, Gerdy tubercle, iliotibial band, and fibular head.

incision.text: Begin in the midlateral thigh at the needed proximal level, curve over the lateral condyle, and extend toward Gerdy tubercle when arthrotomy is required; stop just distal to the joint line if it is not.

superficial_interval.text: Divide the iliotibial band once in line with its fibers and the incision to preserve clean edges for repair.

deep_interval.text: Incise vastus-lateralis fascia just anterior to the lateral intermuscular septum, elevate muscle from distal to proximal, ligate perforators, and retract the muscle anteromedially.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, iliotibial band, vastus-lateralis fascia, muscle-septum interval and perforators, lateral periosteum, and optional lateral capsule.

structures_encountered.text: Iliotibial band, vastus lateralis, lateral intermuscular septum, profunda perforators, lateral femur, joint capsule, patellar tendon, and lateral meniscus are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Profunda femoris perforators, periosteal blood supply, lateral superior genicular vessels, lateral meniscus, patellar tendon, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Identify and ligate perforators during proximal elevation and avoid posterior blind dissection across the septum toward the popliteal neurovascular bundle.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract vastus lateralis atraumatically and avoid excessive tension on the patellar tendon during arthrotomy, particularly in osteoporotic bone.

exposure.text: Exposes the lateral distal femur for reduction and plate placement; an optional anterior-third lateral arthrotomy visualizes simple articular fractures.

limitations.text: Medial-condyle and complex complete-articular patterns are poorly visualized and are generally better served by a parapatellar or broader articular exposure.

extensions.text: Extend proximally along the lateral femoral shaft and distally into a lateral arthrotomy as dictated by fracture and plate length.

indications.text: Use for extra-articular fractures and simple lateral articular patterns that can be reduced and plated from the lateral side.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose a parapatellar or alternative exposure for complex bicondylar, medial-condylar, posterior, or highly comminuted articular injuries needing broader visualization.

implant_implications.text: Center the lateral plate on the distal femur, preserve periosteum, obtain appropriate distal subchondral and proximal fixation, and avoid notch or joint penetration.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm mechanical and anatomic alignment, condylar width, articular congruity, plate position, and screw containment on AP, lateral, and oblique views.

closure.text: Close arthrotomy, repair vastus-lateralis fascia, precisely reapproximate iliotibial band, and close subcutaneous tissue and skin.

complications.text: Complications include perforator bleeding, muscle or periosteal devascularization, malalignment, articular malreduction, stiffness, patellar-tendon injury, infection, nonunion, and hardware irritation.

bailouts.text: If medial or posterior articular reduction cannot be assessed, add or convert to a parapatellar or fragment-specific exposure rather than accepting unseen malreduction.

procedure_applications.condition: A simple lateral articular or extra-articular distal femur fracture requires direct lateral reduction and plate fixation

questions.question: Where is vastus lateralis elevated?
questions.answer: From the lateral intermuscular septum, working distal to proximal and retracting it anteromedially.

questions.question: Which vessels commonly require ligation?
questions.answer: Perforating branches of the profunda femoris artery and vein.

questions.question: When can the distal skin incision stop above Gerdy tubercle?
questions.answer: When no arthrotomy or direct joint visualization is required.
